answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The harbor multiplier is published, charged in terrace, and basalt lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 1377 identities would post 2312 proofs and burn roughly 35 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
